events.type: sector move (chip-equipment, test and memory stocks sold off)
events.summary: FORM fell 4.52% on Tuesday to $141.30 (from $147.99) with no company news. The broad chip fund SMH barely moved (-0.22%) and the S&P 500 fund rose (+0.55%), but the narrower group FORM trades with fell hard the same day (Yahoo daily closes): KLA -4.54%, Camtek -4.63%, Onto Innovation -3.60%, Lam Research -3.44%, Teradyne -3.20%, Applied Materials -2.21%, Aehr Test -11.74%, Cohu -0.85% (median of these eight -3.52%, my arithmetic). Memory: SK hynix's US-listed shares -6.39%, Micron -1.73%. NVIDIA, SMH's biggest holding, rose 0.14%, which is why SMH hid the sell-off. Volume was 2,107,900 shares, about 1.6 times the pre-index-change 20-day average of 1,282,230 (my arithmetic). Tier-3 reports said memory stocks fell because investors turned cautious before Samsung's preliminary Q3 results (Thu 10-08) and SK hynix's results (10-27), on a stronger Korean won and bigger worker-bonus provisions, and on unnamed reports of US data-center delays; a tier-3 premarket report also described chips 'taking a breather' after SOXX rose five sessions in a row and NVIDIA hit a record on Monday. No tier-1/2 source explaining the US chip-equipment sell-off was found (search budget ran out).
events.why_it_matters: It shows most of what the pipeline labelled 'company-specific' (-2.92%) was really a chip-equipment/test/memory sell-off that the SMH comparison does not capture: FORM fell about 1 point more than the median peer. Nothing about FormFactor's own business changed.

Memory stocks fell because investors turned cautious before Samsung's preliminary Q3 results (Thu 10-08) and SK hynix's results (10-27): a stronger won and larger bonus provisions could trim profits, and there were unnamed reports of US data-center delays. Chip stocks were also 'taking a breather' after SOXX rose five sessions in a row and NVIDIA hit a record on Monday.

Basic driver: after a fast run (FORM +36% in a month to 10-06; RSI was 72.8 on 10-02), investors took money off chip-equipment and memory-linked stocks ahead of the memory makers' results, which will show whether AI-memory spending keeps rising. FormFactor's extra weakness fits its bigger run-up, its dependence on SK hynix (24.3% of revenue) and the end of index-inclusion buying, but no source says so.

products.name: Probe cards (DRAM/HBM memory, plus foundry and logic chips incl. GPU)
products.what_it_is: A custom-made test head with thousands of microscopic needles that touches every chip while it is still on the silicon wafer, to find the bad ones before they are cut out and packaged. (No new product news in this window; card carried over from the 2026-10-04 research for context, because the move links to its memory customers.)
products.analogy: A bed of nails built to fit one chip design, pressed on the wafer like a stethoscope that listens to every chip at once; a new design needs a new card and cards wear out.
products.buyers: Memory makers (SK hynix 24.3% of Q2 2026 revenue), foundries (TSMC 11.0%), chip designers; per Deutsche Bank (tier 3), NVIDIA GPUs made at TSMC now included.
products.how_it_works: A tester sends signals through the card's needles into each chip's contact pads and reads the answers; bad chips are marked and thrown out before costly packaging. This matters most for HBM, where one bad layer ruins a whole stack.
products.sales: Not disclosed by product in our sources. Proxy: Q2 2026 total revenue $258.2M, of which Systems was $48.5M (call), implying about $209.7M from probe cards (derived arithmetic, 2026-10-04 research). HBM was about two-thirds of DRAM probe-card revenue (call). GPU probe cards: first production units shipping for revenue from Q3 2026 (call); amount not disclosed.
products.stage: HBM/DRAM: shipping in volume. GPU probe cards: shipping first production units (Q3 2026).
products.competition: Technoprobe (Italy; H1 2026 revenue 464.1M euros, +42.4%, per Italian press via search) and Micronics Japan. Both rose on Tuesday in their own markets (Technoprobe +2.79%, Micronics Japan +2.32%, Yahoo data), then Technoprobe fell about 5.97% on Wednesday.
products.why_investors_care: Every new AI chip or HBM generation needs new, harder and pricier cards; memory makers' spending is FormFactor's revenue.
products.watch_next: Samsung preliminary Q3 (10-08), SK hynix results (10-27), FormFactor Q3 (about 10-28): HBM demand, the HBM-to-DDR mix shift management flagged, GPU revenue disclosure.
